classification_reason: The learner's main asks were met: the tooling ends up working, the validator reports 0 errors, the warning baseline shows no new signature, and no note or tracked file changed. Two robustness problems remain. (1) The documented setup cannot recover from a first failure: the documented PYTHON= override failed identically until the half-built .venv was deleted, which no document mentions. (2) The documented `make test-fast` wrote a phantom AMBIGUOUS, needs-attention request into the learner's operations/diagnostics store, visible via `los operations`. The suite also fails 34 tests here, at least 17 because it reads the product author's own repository files.

confusions: README says Python 3.12+ is required, but a bare `make setup` silently uses the system python3 (3.11) and fails only at the pip step, after creating a venv and upgrading pip in it.
After a failed setup, it was unclear why the documented `PYTHON=python3.12` override failed with the same error; pyvenv.cfg claimed 3.12.3 while the python binary was still 3.11.

corrective_steps: Deleted the half-built, gitignored .venv (created by the failed setup a minute earlier, holding no learner data) and re-ran `make setup PYTHON=python3.12`. This is a generic venv workaround, not a product patch.
Ran `make views` to clear the HYGIENE-VIEWS advisory, since generated/ is disposable and rebuilding it is an automatic permission.
Re-ran two failing test files once to confirm the failures are deterministic.
Left the polluted diagnostic trace in place and reported it; nothing was repaired.
consumer.outcome: The learner sees evidence/S01-answer.md. Tooling works on Python 3.12 after a workaround. The validator reports 0 errors and 2 nonblocking neglect advisories, the warning baseline passes, views are rebuilt, and notes are verified unchanged. Two caveats: the product's own fast test suite fails 34 tests here and cannot serve as a health check, and running it left a phantom 'needs attention' request in her `los operations`.
